title: An inexpensive continuous monitor for multiple human hormones

concept.text: The proposed innovation is an affordable, wearable or otherwise minimally burdensome system that continuously and simultaneously measures several human hormones during ordinary life. It would reveal how hormone concentrations rise, fall and pulse over time across multiple endocrine axes—the linked systems that coordinate hormone production and feedback. The goal is dependable measurement of endocrine dynamics outside specialist sampling facilities, rather than occasional laboratory snapshots.

The instrument would need to distinguish chemically different hormones at physiologically relevant concentrations and resolve changes quickly enough for the intended use. Its measurements must remain reliable throughout sustained operation despite interference and sensor drift. If it samples a fluid other than blood, the relationship between that fluid’s measurements and circulating hormone concentrations must be established for each hormone and use. These are requirements of the proposed broader capability; the supplied evidence does not demonstrate a completed system.

A relevant technical foundation is aptamer-enabled electrochemical sensing, in which a molecular recognition element produces an electrical response to a target hormone. The supplied 2019 study used this approach in a robotic reader for luteinizing hormone, or LH, and discussed extending it to multiple hormones and continuous sensing. It establishes an enabling approach, without establishing that this particular architecture can deliver the entire proposed monitor.

significance.text: Dependable continuous monitoring could make the timing of hormone secretion much easier to study. Hormonal pulses can carry information that an isolated concentration measurement misses. The 2019 LH paper described an assessment approach requiring peripheral blood sampling every 10 minutes for at least eight hours, followed by expensive serial immunochemical analysis. That dated example illustrates why capturing endocrine dynamics can impose substantial burdens on patients and researchers.

Conditional impact synthesis: If the proposed monitor achieved comparable biological validity with low cost and acceptable user burden, its direct consequence would be much richer observation of endocrine rhythms during ordinary life. Simultaneous measurements could show how several hormonal signals vary together, expanding research beyond isolated hormones and tightly controlled sampling sessions. Observed correlations and timing relationships would not, by themselves, establish causal interactions between endocrine systems.

Conditional clinical possibilities include detecting abnormalities missed by sparse sampling and supporting decisions that depend on hormone timing or variability. These possibilities require separate validation for each application: more measurements do not automatically produce better diagnoses, treatments or outcomes. The revolutionary potential lies in making dynamic endocrine measurement accessible and dependable; its eventual clinical reach would depend on what those measurements reliably reveal and whether acting on them helps patients. No historical comparison examples were supplied, so a stronger ranking of its revolutionary importance is not justified here.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central missing capability is sustained, simultaneous measurement of multiple hormones with sufficient specificity, sensitivity and temporal resolution for the intended endocrine questions. Success with one hormone does not establish success with chemically different targets or with a panel operating together. The 2019 paper discussed hormone specificity, sensor regeneration, cost and future multiplexing, including the possibility of using multiple single-wire electrodes to measure several hormones in one sample. That proposed extension was not a demonstrated continuous multi-hormone system.

Long-term measurement also requires a stable relationship between hormone concentration and sensor output. The 2019 article identified signal drift reported for electrochemical aptamer-based continuous sensors in whole blood and discussed regeneration as an engineering concern. A practical monitor must distinguish real hormonal changes from changes in sensor behavior, maintain useful performance through repeated measurements, and control interference without relying on burdensome laboratory procedures.

Engineering synthesis: Biological interpretation is a separate barrier from analytical detection. A sweat or other non-blood sensor could accurately measure its sampled fluid while still failing to reproduce the concentration or timing of a circulating hormone. Hormone-specific relationships, delays and variation across relevant conditions therefore need testing. Simultaneous sensing, calibration, data interpretation, sustained operation and acceptable total cost must work together. The supplied 2019 study did not investigate sweat-to-blood correspondence, and the supplied material does not establish that these broader barriers have been overcome.

current_state.text: On 20 February 2019, Shaolin Liang and colleagues published “Measuring luteinising hormone pulsatility with a robotic aptamer-enabled electrochemical reader” in Nature Communications. Their RAPTER system measured LH in collected patient serum samples. A larger proof-of-concept evaluation used 441 serum samples from three patient cohorts known to have different LH concentrations and pulsatility profiles, comparing results with a clinical immunochemical assay. This demonstrated a relevant method for reconstructing LH concentration profiles and assessing pulsatility from serial samples.

Those results concerned one hormone measured after blood collection and serum preparation. They did not demonstrate continuous sensing inside the body, ordinary-life wearable monitoring or measurement across multiple endocrine axes. Continuous sensing and multiplexing appeared as future adaptations in the discussion. The supplied review’s assessment relied on full article prose and captions, particularly the clinical comparison results and Clinical samples methods; figures were not visually inspected. Figure 3 characterized the electrode and was not the principal evidence for the patient-sampling conclusion.

The reconciled research also identifies a paper attributed to Xiaochang Pei and colleagues, “A quantitative, multimodal wearable bioelectronic device for comprehensive stress assessment and sub-classification,” dated 29 January 2026. It records an earlier abstract-based account of physiological measurements combined with sweat-cortisol sensing. However, the retained PubMed page available to the supplied review contained only a cookie-access message. The review could not verify the article’s identity, measurements, continuity of operation or validation from that content. The reported findings therefore remain an unverified lead within this record; the access failure is not evidence that the findings are false.

Evidence-bound assessment: The supplied material establishes the dated 2019 technical foundation, but it does not establish the field’s overall status as of 1 November 2026. The freshness record was empty, and the retained 2026 page did not contain scientific content. Even if the earlier account of sweat-cortisol sensing is accurate, measuring several physiological modalities alongside one hormone would not alone demonstrate continuous monitoring of multiple circulating endocrine axes. This record consequently cannot determine whether the full proposed capability remains unmet throughout the field.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: An inexpensive, wearable or otherwise minimally burdensome system continuously and simultaneously measures a specified panel of validated hormones spanning at least two endocrine axes during ordinary life. Before testing, investigators should define the panel, monitoring duration, intended applications, acceptable user burden and total cost. The two-axis threshold is a proposed way to demonstrate breadth beyond a single hormone, not an established consensus standard.
completion_criteria.label: Continuous simultaneous hormone monitoring spans at least two endocrine axes

completion_criteria.text: Proposed analytical and temporal validation: Prespecify hormone-specific criteria for concentration accuracy, timing, drift and interference, and test them against reference blood measurements across the physiological and disease ranges relevant to each intended application. Any use of a different sampled fluid should include explicit validation of its relationship to circulating concentrations and timing. Testing should establish sustained simultaneous performance over the claimed monitoring period, so that isolated successful readings or separate single-hormone experiments do not substitute for the integrated capability.
completion_criteria.label: Validate sustained simultaneous hormone measurements against prespecified blood-reference criteria

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: Independent studies should reproduce the claimed performance and report where it deteriorates or fails, including limits of the hormone panel, concentration range, monitoring duration, sampled-fluid interpretation and ordinary-life conditions. Affordability and burden should be evaluated for the complete monitoring process, including recurring supplies, calibration and specialist support where needed. Finite studies would establish demonstrated breadth within those boundaries, not universal performance across every hormone, person or condition.
completion_criteria.label: Independently reproduce performance, reporting practical boundaries and complete monitoring costs

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical validation: For claims that monitoring improves care, clinical studies should show improved outcomes for at least some clearly specified monitoring-guided decisions. Analytical reliability establishes the measurement capability; clinical benefit requires evidence that using the information improves decisions and patient outcomes. These proposed criteria extend the candidate’s completion demonstration and are not requirements established by the 2019 study.
completion_criteria.label: Monitoring-guided decisions improve patient outcomes in clinical studies

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: END-04, “A predictive theory of interacting endocrine control systems,” is the closest conceptual complement. END-03 would supply time-resolved observations that could help develop and test such a theory. END-04 would seek explanations and predictions about interactions and feedback. Reliable measurement alone does not provide a predictive theory, and a theory does not establish a practical monitor.

Roster-based synthesis: END-01, “Immune-protected, renewable human islets that restore autonomous glucose regulation,” END-02, “A general platform for replacing failed endocrine glands with feedback-responsive tissue,” END-07, “Regenerate a person’s own functional pancreatic beta cells,” and END-08, “Restore ovarian endocrine function without previously banked tissue,” concern restoring hormone-producing tissue or gland function. END-03 could potentially help characterize their hormone output and feedback behavior if its validated panel were appropriate. It would measure function rather than supply replacement tissue, regeneration or immune protection.

Roster-based synthesis: END-05, “Durable, safe resetting of dysfunctional energy-balance regulation,” and END-06, “Programmable tissue-selective control of hormone action,” concern changing physiological regulation or the effects of hormones in selected tissues. Multi-hormone monitoring could potentially help assess responses, but circulating hormone concentrations alone do not fully determine tissue-specific action or demonstrate durable resetting of a regulatory system.

Roster-based synthesis: END-09, “Glucose-responsive insulin that substantially automates insulin dosing,” concerns a therapy whose insulin availability or action responds to glucose. END-03 concerns measurement and would not itself provide that therapeutic response. END-10, “Induce durable antigen-specific tolerance in autoimmune endocrine disease,” concerns changing the immune response that contributes to endocrine damage. Monitoring could potentially help assess endocrine function during either intervention, but it would not establish automated insulin dosing or antigen-specific immune tolerance. These entries remain distinct innovations.

unresolved_issues: The identity, findings and validation scope of the cited 2026 wearable study remain unverified from the retained scientific content. The earlier abstract-based account and later access failure cannot be reconciled further from the supplied inputs.
The supplied evidence does not establish the field’s overall status as of 1 November 2026 or whether another system has achieved the proposed capability.
The intended hormone panel, endocrine axes, monitoring duration, applications, acceptable user burden and definition of inexpensive remain unspecified.
Hormone-specific accuracy, timing, drift and interference tolerances, and any sampled-fluid relationship to circulation, remain to be defined and demonstrated.
Which monitoring-guided decisions would improve clinical outcomes remains an application-specific research question.
No historical comparison examples were supplied, so comparative revolutionary importance cannot be calibrated beyond the stated conditional consequences.

brief.title: Affordable, continuous tracking of several hormones
possible: People could follow several hormones as they rise, fall and pulse during everyday life, using an affordable wearable or another system that causes little disruption. They could see patterns that occasional blood tests miss.
why: Researchers could study how hormonal signals vary together outside specialist sampling sessions. Patients could face less burdensome testing when the timing of hormone release matters.
Clinicians could detect abnormalities missed by occasional samples and use hormone timing to guide care.

sources.showed: Their robotic reader measured luteinising hormone, a reproductive hormone, in collected blood samples and reconstructed its pulses. It used aptamers, DNA molecules that bind a chosen target and trigger an electrical response.
sources.quote: Through selective evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment (SELEX), we identify DNA aptamers that bind specifically to LH and not to related hormones.
sources.cited_for: The work supports selective hormone measurement and reconstruction of hormone pulses from repeated blood samples.
sources.not_established: It did not demonstrate continuous monitoring in the body or simultaneous measurement of several hormones during everyday life.

sources.showed: They built a wristband-like device that continuously combines sweat-cortisol sensing with measurements of body signals to assess stress. Cortisol is a hormone involved in the stress response.
sources.quote: This device features exceptional environmental stability, reusability, and fully wireless data and power operation.
sources.cited_for: The work supports combining wearable hormone sensing with other continuous measurements.
sources.not_established: It does not establish continuous measurement of several hormones or their correspondence to blood concentrations and timing.

shown: Liang and colleagues reconstructed reproductive hormone pulses from collected blood samples. Pei and colleagues built a wearable combining sweat-cortisol sensing with body signals. These demonstrate parts of the capability, but neither establishes continuous tracking of several hormones.
missing: A low-burden, affordable system must measure several hormones together throughout everyday use.
Measurements must stay accurate despite interfering substances and changes in sensor response over time.
For measurements outside blood, each hormone’s concentration and timing must be related reliably to its levels in blood.
Independent studies must reproduce performance, and clinical studies must show whether using the measurements improves patient outcomes.

milestones.label: Continuous tracking across distinct hormone control systems
milestones.explanation: An affordable, low-burden monitor would have to track hormones across at least two linked hormone control systems during ordinary life. This would establish breadth beyond an isolated hormone.

milestones.label: Sustained measurements agree with blood references
milestones.explanation: Simultaneous readings would have to meet predefined blood-reference standards for accuracy, timing, interference and sensor stability throughout use. This would establish that the combined measurements are dependable.

milestones.label: Independent studies reproduce performance and establish practical limits
milestones.explanation: Independent studies would have to reproduce performance and report failures, user burden and complete monitoring costs. This would establish where the monitor works and whether people can afford to use it.

milestones.label: Monitoring-guided care improves patient outcomes
milestones.explanation: Clinical studies would have to show that specified decisions guided by monitoring improve patient outcomes. This would establish that the extra information benefits care.

uncertain: Which hormones, monitoring duration, user burden and total cost would make the system useful and affordable?
What accuracy and timing standards should each hormone meet, and how should measurements outside blood be interpreted?
Which decisions guided by continuous hormone measurements would improve patient outcomes?

page.title: Continuous multiplex hormone monitoring
page.definition: A biosensor directly measures at least four hormones in the same person during everyday life, using a fluid such as sweat, saliva or the fluid between tissue cells. It follows the same panel for at least seven consecutive days, measuring each hormone often enough to resolve its changes and secretion pulses, the brief rises in concentration caused by episodic release. Designs include skin-worn and implanted sensors.

goal.need: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome, formerly called polycystic ovary syndrome, affects an estimated 10–13% of women of reproductive age. Profiling luteinising hormone pulses has required blood sampling every 10 minutes for at least eight hours, with about £1,000 in assay charges per patient at 2019 prices. A single draw misses the timing of estradiol and progesterone rises relative to one another. Following such patterns between visits could help clinicians assess treatment response. Repeated androgen tests alone have limited value in adult follow-up.

figures.caption: Requirements for the LH pulsatility assessment described in 2019.
figures.note: LH means luteinising hormone. These figures describe the cited protocol, not a universal diagnostic requirement.

statements.body: SPRIND — German Federal Agency for Breakthrough Innovation
statements.quote: What we need are sensors that measure continuously in everyday life.
Sensors for continuous monitoring of nutritionally relevant small hormones or peptide hormones, such as insulin and glucagon
statements.context: Funding announcement PAR-20-134 included hormone changes during dietary interventions. It specified neither a four-hormone panel nor a seven-day recording.

completion.title: A biosensor resolves at least four hormones’ changes over at least seven consecutive days.
completion.criterion: Directly measure at least four hormones in a biological fluid during everyday life for at least seven consecutive days. Sample each hormone often enough to preserve its biological dynamics and secretion pulses. For a defined women’s-health application, demonstrate a decision that the resulting clinical-grade data enable and that single-point measurements cannot support.
completion.set_by: SPRIND, Continuous Hormone Monitoring Challenge description and call announcement.
completion.threshold_quote: Every team must demonstrate that high-quality continuous hormone data within their specific application area in women’s health enables decisions that are structurally unattainable through single-point measurements.
completion.basis: SPRIND sets the panel size, consecutive duration, temporal resolution and application requirement. Zhou et al. report a four-hormone patch, an exercise-related testosterone rise and five days of signal stability during wear. Lee et al. measured two hormones over 28 days using a fresh sweat patch at each time point. Neither report demonstrates a continuous seven-day record resolving four hormones.

milestones.title: A hormone-sensing prototype quantifies its target in biological material it collects.
milestones.criterion: Use biological material collected by the prototype to demonstrate that it can quantify its target hormone.
milestones.set_by: NIH, PAR-20-134, R21 milestone examples. This is a general device-development criterion in a programme that explicitly includes hormone sensors.
milestones.threshold_quote: biological material retrieved by the devices to establish the initial functionality

milestones.title: The prototype consistently measures its target hormone in the intended study population.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate in people representative of the intended study population that the prototype consistently measures the target hormone under the conditions specified for the clinical investigation.
milestones.set_by: FDA, December 2023 digital-health guidance, section IV.C. This is a general, nonbinding validation criterion, not a hormone-specific authorisation.
milestones.threshold_quote: consistently and appropriately measured in the population of interest.

milestones.title: A hormone monitor meets its measurement specifications against reference measurements.
milestones.criterion: Compare the monitor’s hormone readings with reference measurements under its specified calibration and use conditions. Demonstrate that the readings meet the device’s expected accuracy and precision specifications.
milestones.set_by: FDA, December 2023 digital-health guidance, section IV.C.1. Its general verification criterion is applied here to hormone measurements.
milestones.threshold_quote: Verification confirms that the DHT meets its expected performance specifications.

milestones.title: The integrated monitor meets its prespecified multiplex measurement goals in a human clinical trial.
milestones.criterion: Complete a human clinical trial of the integrated monitor. Analyse the hormone data collected by the device and demonstrate that it meets the protocol’s prespecified functional endpoints for monitoring the panel together.
milestones.set_by: NIH, PAR-20-134, R33 milestone examples. The programme requires application-specific goals rather than a common hormone panel, duration or accuracy cutoff.
milestones.threshold_quote: Data collection and analysis of the biological material collected by the devices, demonstrating the successful completion of the proposed goals.

milestones.title: A prototype produces a detection signal for a target hormone.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate an initial sensor signal in response to a target hormone as proof of the sensing principle.
milestones.set_by: SPRIND, technical detection component of Stage 1 of the Continuous Hormone Monitoring Challenge.
milestones.threshold_quote: established proof of concept, demonstrated initial detection signals

not_found: No numerical affordability threshold was found in the SPRIND challenge, NIH funding announcement or FDA guidance.
No located report established the complete four-hormone, seven-consecutive-day SPRIND test.
Zhou et al.’s full text could not be opened; human enrolment counts and complete on-body validation conditions remain unverified.
No numerical sensor-performance cutoffs for advancement from SPRIND Stage 1 or Stage 2 were located in the challenge materials.
No programme or professional-society statement was located disputing the value or feasibility of the four-hormone, seven-day goal itself.

results.finding: Stressomic’s three hormone sensors were compared with sweat ELISA using 21 biological replicates.
results.detail: The text reports reference validation and calibration-related testing, but does not state quantitative accuracy or precision results against predefined specifications. It does not establish seven-day accuracy or hormone-specific delays.

results.finding: The prototype cortisol electrode showed a sensitivity of 0.2447 µA/log[nM] in buffer across 3 technical replicates.
results.quote: achieving a sensitivity of 0.2447 µA/log[nM] and a high correlation coefficient

results.finding: The SQC-SAS wearable measured a morning peak of 105 nM cortisol in sweat it collected from 1 participant.
results.quote: in the morning, cortisol levels (MSB signal) peaked at 105 nM, consistent with circadian rhythms, and fell to 79 nM after waking up.

results.finding: Wearable and commercial ELISA cortisol readings had an R² of 0.99 across 4 human sweat samples.
results.detail: The bench repeatability tests measured variation in electrode current. The paper does not establish that on-body concentration readings meet a specified precision target.
results.quote: The regression analysis reveals an R² value of 0.99, indicating a high level of correlation between the results from our device and the gold-standard measurement method.

results.finding: The SQC-SAS wearable collected sweat cortisol data from 15 participants who each performed the stress tests twice.
results.detail: The study population is interpreted as volunteers for the reported stress investigation. The paper gives no per-participant measurement success rate.
results.quote: To account for intra-subject variability in these tests for further ML analysis, each test was performed two times by each subject, where the mental arithmetic task was used in one session and the Stroop test in the other as the cognitive stress test.

results.finding: The wire-based LH aptamer sensor achieved a 10.9 nM detection limit in buffer across three replicates.
results.quote: The sensor achieved a limit of detection (LOD) in PBS buffer of 10.9 nM, with a dynamic range of 5–500 nM.

results.finding: RAPTER quantified LH in 441 serum samples from nine women.
results.detail: The robot handled serum after it had been prepared and loaded onto the plate.
results.quote: Having shown that RAPTER can reliably operate with clinical, undiluted patient samples, a larger-scale evaluation was performed using 441 serum samples from three patient cohorts known to have different LH concentrations and pulsatility profiles as a proof-of-concept experiment

results.finding: RAPTER LH readings from nine women and 441 paired serum samples had an R² of 0.94 against clinical immunoassay.
results.detail: The reported coefficients of variation in the clinical laboratory methods describe the reference assay.
results.quote: The RAPTER assay shows a good overall correlation with the clinical immunochemical assay (R 2  = 0.94) (Fig.  5c ).

results.finding: RAPTER repeatedly measured serum LH in nine women over an 8-hour clinical sampling protocol.
results.detail: RAPTER assayed the serial serum samples ex vivo.
results.quote: Furthermore, the RAPTER was able to detect the change in pulsatile LH secretion as reflected by the appropriate measurement of variable levels of LH within a patient’s 8-h clinical study and with subsequent confirmation by BSA analysis.

results.finding: Stressomic immunosensors (n = 3) produced concentration-dependent signals for three target hormones in buffered standards.
results.quote: The competitive binding assay results in an MB reduction peak inversely proportional to hormone concentrations.

results.finding: Stressomic quantified three hormones in sweat collected by its own on-body patch. Participant count unspecified.
results.detail: The integrated patch generated the Fig. 5 on-body results. The separate Fig. 4 pilot used sweat collected with the Macroduct system.
results.quote: After being calibrated in real time using simultaneously collected electrolyte and pH information, the acquired data were converted to the concentration levels based on the calibration curve.

results.finding: Stressomic immunosensor readings were compared with ELISA in 21 human sweat biological replicates.
results.detail: The reference comparison used separately collected sweat. The authors also observed occasional shifts in absolute current across experimental runs.
results.quote: The sensor accuracy was validated against the laboratory standard enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA)

results.finding: Stressomic tracked sweat hormone changes under three stress protocols in healthy participants. On-body sample size unspecified.
results.detail: The reported group sizes for the separate sweat-sample pilot do not establish the size of the integrated wearable cohort.
results.quote: The sensor successfully captured real-time changes in stress hormone levels, showing substantial increases in Cort and NE in response to HIIT and a notable increase in NE level following emotional stimuli

results.finding: Integrated Stressomic produced profiles for a three-hormone sweat panel in an on-body evaluation. Participant count unspecified.
results.detail: In the supplement evaluation, the patch reported decreases in cortisol, epinephrine, and norepinephrine.
results.quote: In the final study, the participant applied the Stressomic patch 10 min after the supplement intake, which reported a reduction in all three stress hormone levels

results.finding: Wearable estradiol readings correlated with ELISA at r = 0.866 across 10 matched buffered sweat samples.
results.detail: The estradiol correlation had a 95% confidence interval of 0.52–0.97. Correlation measures association, and the inter-batch coefficient of variation characterizes sensing-channel reproducibility.
results.quote: Finally, buffered sweat measurements showed good agreement with ELISA reference measurements, with correlation coefficients of r = 0.866 for E2 (slope = 1.011, intercept = −0.82) and r = 0.829 for P4 (slope = 0.922, intercept = −7.45)

results.finding: In two volunteers over approximately one menstrual cycle, wristband sweat estradiol and progesterone profiles tracked paired ELISA trends.
results.detail: The text gives no participant characteristics, numerical agreement statistics, or measurement success rates.
results.quote: The platform was evaluated in two volunteers over approximately one complete menstrual cycle, and the longitudinal E2 and P4 profiles obtained by the wearable sensors showed similar temporal trends to those obtained by paired sweat enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) measurements.

results.finding: In sweat it collected on-body from three women, the wearable aptamer patch quantified oestradiol up to 37.98 pM.
results.detail: The patch calibrated its readings using pH, ionic strength and skin temperature. The separate ELISA comparison used sweat collected with a Macroduct system.
